p: If anyone in your group is nervous about heights, don't worry. Clip 'n Climb is set up to let people go at their own pace, with walls of different difficulty so there's always an easier option. Many people find that once they've made one climb and felt the auto-belay lower them gently back to the floor, the nerves disappear and the fun kicks in. Encouragement from the ground goes a long way, so cheer each other on.

Climbing is a full-body workout, so you'll probably be surprised at how tired your arms get. Take short breaks between walls, keep a drink handy and don't try to do the hardest challenges straight away. Pacing yourself means you'll get more climbs out of your session. Spectators can usually watch, which makes it a nice outing for families where not everyone wants to climb.

Crawley makes a great base for a day out in West Sussex. Gatwick Airport is right on the doorstep, which makes this a handy activity if you're staying nearby before a flight. For something green, Buchan Country Park offers peaceful woodland walks and ponds, while the Hawth theatre puts on shows, concerts and pantomimes in a woodland setting. Further afield, Wakehurst, the wild botanic garden of Kew near Ardingly, is a beautiful place to explore, with gardens, woodland and the Millennium Seed Bank. The old High Street in Crawley's historic centre also has a few characterful buildings, cafés and pubs worth a look.
